lines.trans: I believe there is a problem with Japan's current social climate.
Japan has a culture of modesty, yet there is no need to be bound by it.
My personal theme is love.
Man, I still cannot get used to how everyone looks now.
Ah, delicious. Real miso soup.
Kuroki has changed so much. Why is she talking so formally?
What about my bail money? How did you put it together?

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: Half of it came from the sales of her video.
Just how much did it sell?
Roughly fifty million yen, and sales are still climbing.
I will pay the rest back with interest. Everyone will work nonstop from now on.
Once we finish eating, we are heading out to celebrate.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: social trend; prevailing attitude or climate
meanings.note: Refers to the general mood or tendency in society.

examples.text: 最近の風潮が変わってきた。
examples.trans: Recent social trends have started to change.

examples.text: そういう風潮に流されたくない。
examples.trans: I don't want to be swept up in that kind of trend.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Used for social/work issues as well as test questions.

examples.text: それは大きな問題です。
特に問題はありません。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Derived from the verb 恥じる (to feel shy/ashamed).

examples.text: 彼女には恥じらいがある。
examples.trans: She has a sense of modesty.

meanings.note: Refers to the customs, arts, and social institutions of a group.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.en: to tie; to bind; to restrict
meanings.note: Often used figuratively in the passive 縛られる ('to be bound by').

examples.text: ルールに縛られたくない。
examples.trans: I don't want to be bound by rules.
Tie up the luggage with string.

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Loanword from German 'Thema'.

examples.text: 今日のテーマは愛です。
新しいテーマを決める。

meanings.note: Noun.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Conversational interjection.

examples.trans: Oh dear, we're in a bind.

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: 話してきます combines 話して ('talk and') with きます ('come back') to mean 'I will go talk to them and return'.

examples.text: 少し社長と話してきます。
examples.trans: I will go talk with the president for a bit.

examples.text: ゆっくり話しましょう。

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

examples.text: 来月までに保釈金の一億、死ぬ気で集めてこい！
examples.trans: Scrape together the one hundred million yen bail by next month with everything you have!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

examples.text: 半分はこの売り上げです。
examples.trans: Half of it came from the sales of her video.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.

examples.trans: There is fifty million yen inside.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

examples.text: およそ五千万。でもまだまだ伸びてますよ。
examples.trans: Roughly fifty million yen, and sales are still climbing.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Godan transitive verb.

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Ichidan verb; causative 食べさせる can mean 'to feed/support'.

examples.text: 朝ごはんを食べましたか。
家族を食べさせるために働く。
examples.trans: I work to support my family.

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: 会議は何時に終わりますか。
examples.trans: What time does the meeting end?

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

examples.text: 食べ終わったら祝いに行きますよ。
examples.trans: Once we finish eating, we are heading out to celebrate.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
